content_voiceover: This slide is a classic board matching exercise: connect each lymphoid malignancy to its prognostic and staging system. Start with the universals. Lugano is your general anatomic staging system for lymphoma, and Lugano also defines treatment response criteria, while I-M-W-G response criteria belong to myeloma. Now go disease by disease. For diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, know cell-of-origin, germinal center versus non-germinal center, assigned by the Hans algorithm on immunohistochemistry, plus the International Prognostic Index and its variants: revised I-P-I, N-C-C-N I-P-I, and the C-N-S I-P-I that predicts central nervous system relapse. Follicular lymphoma pairs with FLIPI and FLIPI-2, and the GELF criteria define high tumor burden, meaning who needs treatment versus watchful waiting. Mantle cell lymphoma is MIPI. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia is prognosticated by cytogenetics, TP53, and IGHV mutation status, but staged clinically by Rai and Binet. Hodgkin lymphoma uses the International Prognostic Score. Waldenstrom uses the ISS for Waldenstrom, ISSWM. Peripheral T-cell lymphoma uses I-P-I, the PIT, and the T-cell score. And myeloma is risk-stratified by cytogenetics and staged by the ISS, revised ISS, and the newer R-2-ISS.
keypoints: General: Lugano staging + response; IMWG = myeloma response
FL: FLIPI, FLIPI-2; GELF = tumor burden/when to treat. MCL: MIPI
CLL: del/TP53/IGHV prognosis; Rai & Binet staging. HL: IPS
WM: ISSWM. PTCL: IPI/PIT/T-cell score. Myeloma: ISS/R-ISS/R2-ISS + cytogenetics
keypoint_voiceover: Key associations to lock in: Lugano for general staging and response, I-M-W-G for myeloma response. DLBCL, use the Hans algorithm and the I-P-I family, including C-N-S I-P-I. Follicular is FLIPI, with GELF telling you when to treat. Mantle cell is MIPI. C-L-L uses TP53 and IGHV for prognosis but Rai and Binet for staging. Hodgkin is I-P-S, Waldenstrom is ISSWM, T-cell lymphoma is I-P-I, PIT, and T-cell score, and myeloma is the ISS series.
